source_artifacts.locator: agent card for payments-agent (as consumed by the orchestrator)

capabilities.target: payments-agent: pay vendor from task details (bank account + amount)

inputs.source: Employee purchase request via SSO-authenticated channel
Vendor quote emails and attachments, arriving from outside the company

instructions.note: The prompt states 'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks,' but runtime notes confirm payments-agent performs no verification and pays whatever bank details are in the task. The prompt's assurance of downstream safety does not correspond to any real control.

Instructs the agent to 'use the bank details from the chosen quote' with no instruction to verify those details against the vendor's known payment record. The 'approved list' check appears to validate vendor identity/name only, not the payment destination, which is the actual sink.

The workflow treats manager approval of the purchase request as sufficient authority to carry the task through vendor selection and payment, even though that approval occurs before any quote exists and its record is never passed to payments-agent.

elements.name: A2A task delegation channel from orchestrator to payments-agent

controls.name: Manager approval of the purchase request (item and budget, pre-quote)
controls.decay_rationale: Human approval is independent of model capability, but it approves only the item and budget before any vendor quote exists, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent. It does not cover the vendor-selection or bank-detail decision that actually executes payment.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement relies on the model checking vendor name/identity against the approved list. It does not verify that bank account details in the quote belong to that vendor, and a more capable model facing a convincing spoofed or compromised quote can rationalize a match.

controls.name: Bank-detail confirmation bound to vendor system of record, with approval context propagated to payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: If implemented, payment would be validated against a trusted, write-protected vendor payment record rather than details in an inbound email, and would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Signed and pinned agent card for payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning/signing would prevent silent redefinition or impersonation of the payments-agent endpoint and skill schema after initial trust is established.

controls.name: Mutual authentication / signed per-task identity between orchestrator and payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Would replace the shared static bearer token, which is currently trusted as sufficient authority by payments-agent regardless of which task or requester it carries.

controls.name: Per-vendor / per-period spend cap enforced outside the model
controls.decay_rationale: Would narrow the blast radius of a single fraudulent payment but would not by itself close the path.

controls.name: Audit log of payment tasks and bank-detail changes per vendor
controls.decay_rationale: Detective only; would not prevent a fraudulent payment but would allow earlier detection if reviewed.

findings.title: TC7 Authority laundering / BEC payment fraud: untrusted quote supplies bank details that reach an irreversible payment, while the only human approval covers a different decision

attack_path.note: External, untrusted email quote arrives containing attacker-controllable bank account details.
Quote is compared against the approved vendor name list; this does not check payment destination.
The only human approval occurred earlier, for item and budget, before any quote existed, and its record is not passed forward.
Orchestrator hands the bank details from the chosen quote to payments-agent for payment.
Pays the bank details in the task with no independent verification, trusting the orchestrator's bearer token as sufficient authority.

findings.residual_rationale: The only credited control (ctl.approved_vendor_only_instruction) is behavioral/dependent and checks vendor name identity, not whether the bank account in the quote matches that vendor's known payment details, which is the exact element the attack manipulates. The rubric's step-4 credit would float residual to high, but that credit does not address the actual sink, so residual is kept at the inherent ceiling.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or prompt version change; any removal or loosening of the vendor-list check; approval workflow changed to skip manager review of the purchase request.

evidence.observation: The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists. The approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.
Use the bank details from the chosen quote. Only pay vendors on the approved list.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company.

recommendations.action: Bind payment execution to bank/account details confirmed in a trusted, write-protected system of record for the approved vendor; reject or escalate for human review any payment where the quote's bank details differ from the vendor's record.

Propagate the manager's approval context, including the specific vendor and bank details that were approved, to payments-agent, and require payments-agent to verify the task matches that approved record before paying.
Log and alert on any payment task whose bank details differ from previously used details for the same vendor.
Add a per-vendor and per-period spend cap enforced outside the model.

findings.title: ASI04/ASI07: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card and shared static bearer trust enable impersonation or silent redefinition of the payment peer (SAFE-T1004)

attack_path.note: Agent card is fetched at startup, is not signed, and is not pinned to a known-good version.
Orchestrator delegates payment tasks to whatever endpoint and skill definition the card currently presents, authenticated only by a shared static bearer token.

evidence.observation: Card specifies only a bearer authentication scheme, with no signature or pin mentioned.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.

forecast.watch_signal: Any change to payments-agent's endpoint URL or card contents between startups, or addition of further A2A peers reusing the same unpinned trust pattern.

recommendations.action: Pin and verify payments-agent's agent card by signature or hash; reject unsigned or changed cards without re-approval.
Replace the shared static bearer token with mutual TLS or signed, per-task identity assertions between orchestrator and payments-agent.

rating.rationale: The dominant path is an untrusted vendor quote email supplying attacker-controllable bank details directly into an irreversible, shared-credential payment delegation (S3 sink), with the only human approval covering a different, earlier decision and not propagated to the paying agent. The single credited control (an approved-vendor-name instruction) is behavioral, dependent, and does not check the actual exploited field (bank details), so residual is held at critical rather than floored down. A secondary, independent finding (unsigned/unpinned A2A peer with static bearer trust) sits at high and does not change the rollup. Both findings already sit at or near their ceiling, so the forecast equals the residual; the single control whose decay matters most is ctl.approved_vendor_only_instruction, which a more capable or longer-running model can route around via a convincing spoofed or compromised vendor quote.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/A2A transport configuration, IaC, or payments-agent source code was provided; the agent-card and protocol findings are inferred from the card contents and runtime notes, so confidence on finding f2 is medium.
No logging, audit, or monitoring configuration was described; detective and corrective controls are recorded as missing_recommended rather than verified absent.
